vendors.notes: IBM products (watsonx Orchestrate ADK, UI modernization, Carbon, Client Engineering building blocks) and the marketplace team's own accelerators. Packs are curated by the marketplace team from these official repositories with recorded provenance.

Curated from the public anthropics/skills repository. Only the Apache-2.0 skills are eligible; the document skills (docx, pdf, pptx, xlsx) are source-available with a no-copy licence and stay out of the registry.
Curated from the Codex skills catalog (openai/skills). Each skill carries its own LICENSE.txt; only Apache-2.0 skills are taken.
Curated from google/skills (Apache-2.0): agent skills for Google Cloud, Gemini, Ads and Analytics.
Curated from hashicorp/agent-skills (MPL-2.0): Terraform and Packer skills.
Curated from microsoft/skills (MIT): Azure operations and SDK skills shipped as Claude Code plugins under .github/plugins/.

Curated from confluentinc/agent-skills (Apache-2.0): Kafka clients, Kafka Streams, Schema Registry, Flink and Confluent Cloud pipelines. Confluent has been an IBM company since March 2026 and keeps its own GitHub organisation, so it is listed as its own vendor, like HashiCorp.

Curated from openshift/agentic-skills (Apache-2.0), the skills OpenShift maintainers publish for OpenShift Lightspeed: cluster update readiness, Red Hat product life cycle and Argo CD GitOps. Red Hat is an IBM company and keeps its own GitHub organisations, so it is listed as its own vendor, like HashiCorp and Confluent.

packs.name: agent-evals
packs.description: Test a deployed watsonx Orchestrate agent through its API and see every tool it called, with arguments, results and hand-offs. Cases in IBM's AgentOps Core format, runs that wait for your yes, offline scoring, Bob as the judge, and a report.

skills.name: wxo-agent-api
skills.description: Call a deployed watsonx Orchestrate (wxo) agent from Python and get its answer with every tool call, tool result, hand-off and timing, through a small standard-library client. A one-time probe shows where the instance exposes tool calls; scripts ask an agent one or more questions or a CSV batch of them, and custom scripts build on the same client. Nothing reaches the agent before the user's yes. Use when the user wants to call or test a wxo agent from code, see which tools an agent run called, script against the Orchestrate runs API, or asks whether the API returns tool calls without streaming. Triggers include "call my Orchestrate agent from Python", "get the tool calls of a wxo agent run", "are tool calls only in the stream", "batch questions to my wxo agent", "напиши скрипт, который вызывает агента wxo", "где в API видны вызовы тулов", "проверь, как агент отвечает через API", "прогони вопросы из CSV через агента wxo".

skills.name: wxo-eval-cases
skills.description: Write and check evaluation test cases for a deployed watsonx Orchestrate (wxo) agent in IBM's AgentOps Core format - a skeleton from the user's scenario, a draft from a real conversation thread, validation against the agent's tool catalog and argument schemas, and an export folder and ZIP for `orchestrate evaluations` and the server-side upload. Reads the tenant only (agents, tools, thread messages); never sends a message to the agent and never uploads. Use to create, draft or check test cases or a golden set for a wxo agent, to turn a good conversation into a regression test, or to prepare cases for `orchestrate evaluations`. Triggers include "write eval cases for my Orchestrate agent", "make a test case from this thread", "validate my wxo test cases", "export cases for IBM agentops", "тест-кейсы для агента wxo", "сделай тест из этого диалога", "проверь тест-кейсы агента Orchestrate".

skills.name: wxo-eval-run
skills.description: Run test cases against a deployed watsonx Orchestrate (wxo) agent and score what it did. Nothing is sent before the user's yes to a read-only plan; one canary case first, the rest after a second yes. Each turn's tool calls, results and hand-offs are captured and scored offline (arguments, order, routing, forbidden tools); Bob judges answer quality with a rubric. Reports in Markdown, HTML and CSV and diffs two runs for regressions. Use when the user wants to run evals for a wxo agent, check a new version for regressions or measure tool-call accuracy. Triggers include "run the evals for my Orchestrate agent", "did the new agent version regress", "tool call accuracy of my wxo agent", "benchmark my wxo agent against test cases", "прогони тесты агента wxo", "оцени агента orchestrate", "сравни два прогона".

safety.warning: Every message sent to the agent creates a run, and usually a thread, on your watsonx Orchestrate tenant, and the agent may call tools that change external systems. The threads stay on the tenant.
safety.covered: Nothing is sent before your yes to a read-only plan or dry run that lists the host, the agent and every tool and collaborator it can reach; the runner then sends one canary case and stops. No script deletes, imports or removes anything, and every thread id is recorded. A forbidden tool is detected after it ran, so use a draft environment and a sandboxed test tenant.

safety.warning: Test prompts go to your tenant, and the saved traces hold prompts, answers and tool outputs that may carry personal data from the agent's backends. If you run exported cases in IBM's own evaluation framework, it sends the transcripts to its judge model.
safety.covered: Traces stay in the project under `agent-evals/runs/` and `agent-evals/probe/raw/`, and the skills suggest git-ignoring both. Bob judges answers in your session, so nothing goes to a third service; export only writes local files. Credentials come from the environment only, and the token stays in memory, never printed or written. Captures become test fixtures only through `probe.py sanitize` and your review.

safety.warning: Agent answers, tool results, thread messages and agent instructions come from the tenant and its backends and can carry text aimed at Bob.
safety.covered: The rule, the skills and the judge rubric treat them as data: quoted, never followed, and an instruction found in an answer is reported as a finding. Turns come from the case file, never from the agent's output, and `report.html` escapes everything.

packs.name: bob-essentials
packs.description: The marketplace inside Bob: find and install packs from chat, audit a skill before anyone trusts it, check the setup from hooks to MCP servers, and write new skills, modes, rules and commands. Ships /skills-add and a security rule that every task follows.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: The Bob Skills Marketplace inside Bob. Use when the user wants a skill or a capability Bob does not have installed, pastes a git link or a repository name and asks to install skills from it, asks what packs or skills exist ("is there a skill for X", "find a skill"), or asks to install, update, remove or explain a marketplace pack. Covers browsing the catalog offline, mapping a git link to a pack, showing what will be installed before confirming, accepting a vendor on first install, and refusing repositories outside the marketplace.

skills.name: skill-creator
skills.description: Create or improve IBM Bob skills (SKILL.md plus optional scripts, references and assets), custom modes, rules and slash commands that Bob picks up and the marketplace policy linter accepts, with safe defaults built in - the user's yes before every external write, outside content treated as data, TLS on, loopback listeners, least-privilege modes. Use when the user wants to write a new skill, package a repeated workflow as a skill, fix a skill Bob ignores, create a custom mode, add a project rule or a slash command, or prepare any of them for a marketplace pack. Triggers include "create a skill", "write a SKILL.md", "package this as a skill", "the skill is not picked up", "create a mode", "add a rule", "make a slash command", "создай скилл", "создай режим".

skills.name: guard
skills.description: Explain and resolve a refusal from the uvx bob-skills guard hook, which checks every skill against .bob/skills.lock before Bob activates it. Use when a skill activation was refused with a "uvx bob-skills guard" message, or the user asks why a skill is blocked, mentions "unmanaged skill", "digest mismatch", "revoked version", "skill blocked", "guard", or wants to trust a local skill again.

skills.name: skill-audit
skills.description: Check a skill before anyone trusts or installs it - a skill copied from a repository, a web page or a colleague, the user's own skill, or an unmanaged skill the guard refused. Runs the marketplace policy linter, plus NVIDIA SkillSpector and Cisco skill-scanner when installed, then reads the skill for the holes scanners miss - writes or admin actions without the user's yes, instructions hidden in content the skill reads, TLS verification off, servers listening on all interfaces, stored credentials reused for unauthenticated requests. Use when the user asks "is this skill safe", "check this skill", "audit the skill", "can I trust it", "проверь скилл", or before `uvx bob-skills trust`.

skills.name: bob-doctor
skills.description: Check the Bob setup of this project and of ~/.bob and fix problems together with the user - guard hook missing, skills modified after install or unmanaged, skills Bob ignores, MCP servers with secrets in the config, unpinned versions, plain HTTP, TLS verification off, listeners on all interfaces, write tools approved in advance or telemetry on, and custom modes with unknown tool groups. Use when the user says "check my Bob setup", "doctor", "why is my skill or MCP server not working", "is my mcp.json safe", "проверь настройки Bob", or after installing packs or adding MCP servers by hand.

packs.name: challenge-kit
packs.displayName: Challenge kit: from the first idea to the submission
packs.description: For teams in an AI coding challenge or hackathon, newcomers and experienced alike. A guided first session, ideas when there is nothing to start from, a process rethought, a scope with invented data, a solution blueprint with an architecture diagram, a usability pass, the demo script and a check before submitting.

skills.name: first-hour
skills.description: A guided first session for someone who has never worked with a coding agent, done on their own challenge task instead of a tutorial. Checks the hackathon setup (the right Bob account, the Bobcoin budget, building inside Bob IDE so the session report exists), then walks through one small real task in five moves - say the goal, give the context, agree a plan, let Bob do one step and read what it did, check the result - and leaves a one-page card of working habits. Use when the user says they are new to Bob or to AI coding assistants, asks how to work with Bob or how to start, seems unsure what to type, or says "never used a coding agent".

skills.name: idea-studio
skills.description: Find a challenge or hackathon idea worth building when there is nothing to start from, or sharpen half an idea. A short interview about the team's own world, then six to eight ideas forced apart across directions (new application, modernisation, Bob with MCP, AI agent) and kinds of value, each with who it helps, the demo moment, the argument for it and its main risk, scored against the four judging criteria, with one recommendation and the reasoning. Renders the ideas as an HTML board to choose from. Use when the user says they have no idea what to build, asks for project or PoC ideas, wants to brainstorm for the Bob challenge or a hackathon, wants to compare several ideas, or says "what should we build".

skills.name: process-redesign
skills.description: Simplify, automate or improve an existing process, and question whether it should exist in its present shape. Interviews the user by slots (outcome, trigger, steps, actors, systems, work time and waiting time, volume, rules, expectations), closes the gaps between what they expect and what can be built, draws the process as lanes with its totals, then proposes two options, one that improves the process and one that replaces it, with an honest comparison, and turns the chosen one into a week-by-week plan for a proof of concept. Use when the user wants to automate or speed up a workflow, describes how something is done today, brings a process document or SOP, asks for a plan to improve a business process, or says "as-is and to-be", "map this process".

skills.name: poc-scope
skills.description: Cut a real, complex case down to a proof of concept that can run in a few weeks without real company data. Chooses the thin slice (one case type carried end to end), sorts every component into real, mocked or out, designs mocks that sit behind the real interfaces so they can be swapped for the system later, and generates invented data with planted cases and an answer key from a small JSON schema. Use when the team wants to build on a real company process or system, asks what to include in the PoC, needs test or demo data, cannot use production data, asks for synthetic data or mocks, or says "scope the PoC".

skills.name: solution-blueprint
skills.description: Write the solution blueprint of a challenge, hackathon or proof-of-concept entry as one impressive, self-contained HTML document with real diagrams - the one number that matters, the process before and after as lanes on a shared time scale, a layered architecture diagram with IBM technology marked, impact as before and after bars and a value waterfall, alternatives, demo storyboard, adoption path, roadmap, the judging criteria answered, risks and assumptions. Every number is marked measured, estimate or assumption, and the document says whether it is a plan or drawn from the working build. Three themes, print to PDF, a presenter mode, right-to-left languages. Use when the user asks for a solution document, a design paper, an architecture diagram, a business case, a one-pager for management, a submission document, or says "blueprint", "write up our PoC".

skills.name: usability-pass
skills.description: Walk a built proof of concept as a first-time user and find what would stop a real one - the first minute, the first screen, empty states, waiting, errors, wording, trust in the result, and for an agent or chat the opening, not knowing, clarifying questions and confirmation before acting. Returns findings rated blocks, slows or polish with the smallest fix for each, a five-minute test script for one real person, the time to first value, and the adoption section of the blueprint. Use when a PoC or demo runs and the user asks whether it is easy to use, wants UX feedback or a usability review, prepares for judging on design and usability, or says "UX review".

skills.name: demo-script
skills.description: Plan the demonstration of a challenge or hackathon entry - one claim, one case carried from start to outcome on the real screen, the single moment the room understands, timings for each step, the demo data and its reset, a prepared answer for every way it can break, a recorded backup and a checklist for the day. Writes the run of show and fills the demo section of the blueprint. Use when the team prepares to show their PoC, asks how to demo, what to show in three minutes, how to prepare for demo day or what to do if the demo fails, or says "demo script", "run of show".

skills.name: submission-check
skills.description: Check a challenge or hackathon entry before it is submitted or its repository is made public. A read-only script looks for credentials in the tracked files and in the git history, for files that should not be tracked, and for the pieces an entry needs (README, blueprint, exported Bob session report, nothing uncommitted); then Bob reads the README as a stranger, checks the files for real company data, and scores the entry against the four judging criteria with evidence to find the weakest one while there is time to act. Reports only - it never rewrites history, rotates a key or pushes. Use before submitting, before making a repository public or pushing it to a public host, when the user asks whether the entry is ready, or says "pre-submission check", "are we ready to submit".

safety.warning: The skills write what you tell them about your company's processes, people, volumes and costs into files under `challenge/`, and a challenge entry is usually submitted as a public repository.
safety.covered: Nothing leaves the machine: the scripts have no network code and the page is one local HTML file. The rule assumes company data may not leave the company, `poc-scope` makes invented data for the build, and `submission-check` looks for credentials and real-looking data before a public push. Credentials never go into a file or a command line, and a found one is shown masked.

safety.warning: The skills read process documents, exports, emails and the files and git history of your repository, and `usability-pass` reads what your running solution shows. Such material can carry text aimed at Bob.
safety.covered: The rule, the mode and each skill treat that material as data: quoted and reported, never followed. The challenge-coach mode can edit only under `challenge/`, the renderer escapes every string of the spec, and the pack changes no code, rewrites no git history, rotates no key, pushes nothing and installs no other pack: those steps are yours.

skills.name: ibmcloud-setup
skills.description: Check and prepare the IBM Cloud CLI before any IBM Cloud work - the CLI version, the plug-ins the ibm-cloud pack uses (VPC, Kubernetes Service, Code Engine), whether a session is open and which account, region and resource group it targets, and whether API tracing is on. Guides federated (SSO) login, where the user types the one-time passcode in their own terminal, and login with an API key from the environment. Use it first in any IBM Cloud task and whenever a command fails with "Not logged in", a missing plug-in or the wrong account. Triggers include "check my IBM Cloud setup", "log in to IBM Cloud", "which IBM Cloud account am I on", "ibmcloud says not logged in", "настрой ibmcloud", "в каком я аккаунте IBM Cloud".

skills.name: ibmcloud-inventory

skills.name: ibmcloud-diagnose

Triggers include "can't connect to my VSI", "port 443 not reachable", "cluster is in warning", "Code Engine app failed", "revision not ready", "не открывается сервер в VPC", "кластер в warning", "приложение Code Engine не стартует".

skills.name: ibmcloud-cost
skills.description: Show where the IBM Cloud money goes, read-only - cost per service, per resource group and per instance for a month, the change against the previous month, the top spenders, and instances billed while their usage is zero, from the IBM Cloud usage reports. Works with the role the user has - account billing access gives the whole account, a resource group administrator gets that group - and names the role needed for anything the role does not allow. Never stops, scales or deletes anything. Use for "how much do we spend on IBM Cloud", "why did the bill go up", "what costs the most", "cost by resource group", "cloud cost report", "сколько мы тратим в IBM Cloud", "почему вырос счёт", "расходы по группам ресурсов".

safety.warning: The skills run the ibmcloud CLI in the session you opened, which carries every right your account gives you. A command outside the pack's read-only set could change or delete resources.
safety.covered: The pack's scripts only list and read. The `ibm-cloud` rule makes every changing command wait for your yes to that exact command, and `cloud-ops` mode writes only under `ibmcloud-reports/`. For the strictest setup, log in with an access group or service ID that has Viewer roles only.

safety.warning: Resource names, tags, event messages and application logs come from the account and can carry text aimed at the agent.
safety.covered: The rule and every skill treat them as data: they are quoted to you, never followed.

packs.name: ibm-watsonx-data-integration
packs.description: Build, run, diagnose and operate data flows in IBM watsonx.data integration (DataStage, pyflow) from natural language: flow lifecycle, DataStage and pyflow authoring, failed-run investigation, engine knowledge and bug reports. IBM's official skills, used with the Agentic Data Integration MCP server on IBM Cloud.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-lifecycle
skills.description: Entry point for ALL flow work in watsonx.data integration — creating, editing, running, diagnosing a failed run, or backing up/restoring a flow. Load this FIRST whenever a request touches a data flow. It gathers intent — including which engine the flow runs on — routes to exactly one lifecycle state, and applies a fixed precedence order so routing is consistent run to run.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-datastage
skills.description: Reference for the verbose watsonx.data integration SDK for DataStage (batch) flows, with exhaustive stage and property access — the full engine stage catalog. Load this only after the di-agent-flow-lifecycle router has selected the datastage-sdk authoring backend — this is a syntax and stage reference, not a decision about whether to use it. If you have not routed yet, load di-agent-flow-lifecycle instead.

skills.name: di-agent-flow-pyflow
skills.description: API spec for pyflow, IBM's LLM-optimized Python DSL for authoring DataStage and StreamSets flows. Its compact surface and compile-time validation offer context efficiency, fast feedback, and correctness guarantees. Load this only after the di-agent-flow-lifecycle router has selected the pyflow authoring backend — this is a language reference, not a decision about whether to use it. If you have not routed yet, load di-agent-flow-lifecycle instead.

skills.name: di-agent-datastage-investigation
skills.description: Deep investigation of a failed run of a DataStage job already in operation — a scheduled or production job, or any job whose failure the user asks you to investigate. Works end-to-end from MCP tools: logs, job config, flow structure, connection health. Produces a root-cause diagnosis, not a fix. NOT for a run that failed while a flow was being built or edited — those are handled by the di-agent-flow-lifecycle skill, which runs its own investigation and loads this one only when a production-depth analysis is needed.

skills.name: di-agent-knowledge-engine-datastage
skills.description: Q&A reference for the DataStage parallel engine — parallelism, partitioning theory, APT configuration files, concurrent job execution, restart/recovery, disk/resource tuning, dataset performance, flow optimization (partitioning/sorting/memory), and per-stage semantics. Use for conceptual engine questions and stage property lookups regardless of authoring tool.

skills.name: di-agent-bug-report
skills.description: Generates a Markdown bug report for an IBM watsonx.data integration session. User can invoke directly. The agent MUST propose it (and must wait for explicit acceptance) after 3 or more consecutive calls to the same tool or the same sequence of tools result in a failure or the same error. Skip for non-watsonx.data integration sessions.

safety.warning: The flow skills run, re-run, restore and delete jobs and assets in your watsonx.data integration instance, and a run whose write mode is `overwrite` truncates the target table.
safety.covered: This pack's rule requires your yes for each run, retry, restore and delete, names the target connections and the write mode first, and treats job logs and data rows as data.

packs.name: office-docs
packs.description: Create, edit, fill and extract Word documents, PowerPoint decks and Excel workbooks from Bob with python-docx, python-pptx and openpyxl. Original IBM skills with tested helper scripts; nothing leaves the machine.

skills.name: docx
skills.description: Create, edit, fill and extract Microsoft Word (.docx) files with python-docx through four ready-made scripts. Build a document from a JSON spec of headings, paragraphs, bullet and numbered lists, tables, images and page breaks (optionally on top of a template that keeps its styles, headers and footers), replace {{placeholders}} in a template even when Word split them across runs, dump the headings, text and tables of a .docx to Markdown or JSON, and convert to PDF with LibreOffice. skills.name: pptx
skills.description: Create, edit, fill, extract and render PowerPoint (.pptx) decks with python-pptx and tested helper scripts. Builds a 16:9 deck from a Markdown outline (title slide, nested bullets, images, native bar/line/pie charts, speaker notes, optional corporate .pptx or .potx template), finds and replaces text across slides and notes while keeping run formatting, dumps an existing deck to Markdown with slide numbers, and renders it to PDF and PNG with LibreOffice for review. skills.name: xlsx

Builds sheets from a JSON spec with a styled frozen header, number formats (currency, percent, date), live formulas, a totals row, autofilter, native bar/line/pie charts and dropdown validation; converts CSV/TSV exports into typed sheets; reports what an existing workbook contains (sheets, header, formulas, charts, names, merged cells); and checks formulas for errors through a LibreOffice recalculation or a static scan. skills.name: pdf
skills.description: Read, create, fill and manipulate PDF files with five ready-made scripts built on pypdf, pdfplumber and reportlab. Extract text per page (page ranges, layout mode, scanned-PDF detection), pull tables out as Markdown or CSV, build a report PDF from a JSON spec (headings, paragraphs, lists, tables, images, page numbers, Unicode font so Hebrew, Arabic and Cyrillic render), merge, split, rotate, watermark, compress, encrypt and set metadata, list and fill AcroForm fields, and OCR scanned pages locally with tesseract and poppler. Not for Word, Excel or PowerPoint files unless a PDF is involved.

packs.name: presentations
packs.description: From a topic or your own data to a deck and the talk around it: one headline per slide, a style picked from five, charts and pictures. The same storyboard builds an interactive HTML deck, a printable PDF and a 16:9 PowerPoint.

skills.name: deck-dataviz

Trigger on: Flink UDF, custom Flink function, process table function, PTF, UDTF, Flink user defined, extend Flink SQL, stateful stream processing with Flink. Do NOT trigger for: Kafka Streams UDFs (use kafka-streams-programming skill), general Flink job development without custom functions, CDC streaming data piplines that include Flink (prefer the confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow skill), Flink connector setup, or Kafka producer/consumer code.

skills.name: confluent-cloud-flink-sql
skills.description: Write and debug Flink SQL that runs on Confluent Cloud, enforcing the CC-vs-Apache-Flink (OSS) dialect boundary. Use when the working directory is a Confluent Cloud Flink workspace, when a Flink SQL statement needs checking before it runs on a CC compute pool, or when the user mentions CC Flink, Confluent Cloud Flink SQL, the `confluent flink` CLI, a CFU compute pool, `CREATE CONNECTION`, or asks to check or debug Flink SQL whose runtime is Confluent Cloud. Also trigger when a Flink SQL question is posed and nothing establishes an Apache Flink OSS runtime. Do NOT trigger for: building or deploying Flink UDFs in Java (UDF/UDTF/PTF — use flink-udf); a full CDC pipeline from a database through Flink into Tableflow/Iceberg/Delta Lake (use confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow); Kafka Streams topology work (use kafka-streams-programming); or Flink SQL confirmed to run on Apache Flink OSS, not Confluent Cloud.

skills.name: confluent-cloud-cdc-tableflow
skills.description: Set up end-to-end Change Data Capture (CDC) pipelines on Confluent Cloud using Debezium source connectors, Flink for transformation, and Tableflow for data lake integration. Supports JSON_SR, Avro, and Protobuf formats. Handles schemaless topics (plain JSON without SR) and multi-event topics. This skill handles the complete workflow from database to Iceberg/Delta tables. Use this skill when users want to capture database changes and materialize them into Iceberg or Delta Lake tables via Confluent Cloud Tableflow. Trigger phrases include "CDC to Tableflow", "database to Iceberg", "database to Delta Lake", "stream database changes to data lake", "set up Tableflow pipeline", "schemaless topic to Tableflow", or "multi-event topic to Iceberg". Do NOT trigger for general CDC, Debezium, or database replication requests that do not involve Tableflow or Iceberg/Delta Lake as the destination.

skills.name: msk-migration
skills.description: Use this skill to assess and plan a migration from AWS MSK (Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka) to Confluent Cloud. Triggers on user intent like "migrate MSK to Confluent Cloud", "move off MSK", "MSK to CC cutover", "Zero-Cut migration from MSK", "kcp scan my MSK", or any discussion of MSK-to-CC assessment, planning, cluster sizing, Cluster Linking setup, Gateway-based switchover, or post-cutover validation. Do NOT trigger for non-MSK Kafka sources (open-source Kafka, Aiven, Confluent Platform, Redpanda) — this skill is MSK-only. Do NOT trigger for greenfield Confluent Cloud projects with no existing Kafka source. Do NOT trigger for general Kafka programming questions (producer/consumer code, Kafka Streams) unrelated to migration.

safety.warning: The Confluent Cloud skills create and delete environments, connectors, topics and Flink statements, and Flink statements consume CFUs while they run.
safety.covered: The skills present a plan and run EXPLAIN before CREATE; the security-defaults rule adds a yes per create or delete, named by object and environment. The teardown script asks once before it deletes the demo topics and local state.

safety.warning: The bundled docker-compose files publish the broker, REST proxy and Schema Registry without authentication on every network interface, and the setup guides write cluster keys into local properties files.
safety.covered: Publish those ports as `127.0.0.1:PORT:PORT` when you run them, and add the key files to `.gitignore` as the Java skill does.

packs.name: redhat-openshift

packs.description: Check whether an OpenShift cluster is ready for an update, look up Red Hat product support phases and compatibility, and debug, audit, operate and onboard teams to Argo CD GitOps. Red Hat's official skills for OpenShift Lightspeed, curated from openshift/agentic-skills.

skills.name: cluster-update-advisor
skills.description: Assess OpenShift cluster update (upgrade) readiness and risk. Use when evaluating whether a cluster is safe to update, when an update is available, or when the user asks about update risks, prerequisites, blockers, or best practices.

skills.name: product-lifecycle
skills.description: Query Red Hat Product Life Cycle data for support phases, end-of-life dates, and OpenShift version compatibility. Use when evaluating whether installed operators or layered products are supported on a given OCP version, approaching end of life, or need upgrading before a cluster upgrade. Also use when the user asks about product support status, EOL dates, or lifecycle phases for any Red Hat product.

skills.name: argo-knowledge
skills.description: Comprehensive knowledge base for the Argo ecosystem including Argo CD, Argo Rollouts, Argo Workflows, and Argo Events. Use this skill when generating, reviewing, debugging, or explaining Argo CRDs (Application, ApplicationSet, AppProject, Rollout, AnalysisTemplate, Workflow, WorkflowTemplate, CronWorkflow, EventSource, Sensor, EventBus), configuring notifications, image updater, sync policies, progressive delivery strategies, or designing GitOps repository patterns. Also use when the user asks about Argo best practices, common mistakes, or needs to choose between Argo approaches (e.g., app-of-apps vs ApplicationSet, canary vs blue-green, steps vs DAG workflows).

skills.name: argo-cluster-debug
skills.description: Debug and troubleshoot the Argo ecosystem on live Kubernetes clusters — inspects Argo CD Application sync status, health checks, and controller logs; diagnoses Argo Rollouts canary/blue-green failures and AnalysisRun results; traces Argo Workflow step failures and artifact issues; and debugs Argo Events EventSource and Sensor connectivity. Prefers argocd/argo CLIs when available, falls back to kubectl for CRD inspection. Use when users report failing, stuck, or degraded Argo resources on a cluster.

skills.name: argo-repo-audit
skills.description: Audit and validate Argo CD GitOps repositories by scanning local repo files (not live clusters) — reviews AppProject RBAC and security restrictions, checks sync policies and operational best practices, optionally runs schema validation, and produces a prioritized GitOps report. Use when users ask to audit, analyze, validate, review, or security-check an Argo CD GitOps repo.

skills.name: argo-operations
skills.description: Set up, deploy, promote, and manage Argo ecosystem resources on live Kubernetes and OpenShift clusters. Covers Argo CD installation (Helm, operator, Autopilot), Application and ApplicationSet lifecycle, Rollout promotion and rollback, and day-2 operations (upgrades, API migration, scaling). Every write operation uses dry-run first and requires explicit user confirmation before applying. Use when users want to install Argo CD, create or sync Applications, promote Rollouts, or perform operational changes on their Argo setup.

skills.name: argo-team-onboard
skills.description: Onboard app teams onto Argo CD with discovery-first workflows. Generates AppProject, Application, and RBAC configuration tailored to the team's existing stack (Helm, Kustomize, or plain YAML). Supports manual single-team onboarding and self-service scaling via ApplicationSet + teams.yaml. Does NOT generate CI pipelines, registry config, or secrets backends — focuses on Argo CD resources only. Use when users ask about onboarding teams, adding tenants, setting up new teams, bootstrapping first apps, or self-service onboarding patterns.

safety.warning: argo-operations and argo-team-onboard install Argo CD, create, sync and roll back Applications and apply AppProjects, RBAC and cluster Secrets; a few reference procedures apply CRDs or remote manifests before their own confirmation step, and the argocd-rbac-cm example replaces the whole policy.
safety.covered: Both skills preview with a server-side dry run and ask before applying. The pack rule adds a yes per command with the kube context named, pinned remote manifests, and a merge instead of the rbac example. cluster-update-advisor only advises and never upgrades.

safety.warning: Logs, events, Application status, readiness JSON and manifests from Git reach Bob as they are, and none of the skills says to treat them as data.
safety.covered: The pack rule and the bob-essentials security-defaults rule make that content data, never instructions; runbooks are read, not executed.

safety.warning: Backup steps write repo and cluster Secrets to local files as plain base64, some steps print Secrets or put tokens on the command line, and the repo audit can copy secret values into its report.
safety.covered: The pack rule forbids printing Secrets, keeps tokens off command lines and output, asks before a backup with Secrets is written to disk, and redacts secret values in audit reports.

safety.warning: argo-operations starts the Argo Rollouts dashboard in the background; it has no authentication and acts with your cluster login.
safety.covered: The pack rule says not to start it or a port-forward on all interfaces, and to bind 127.0.0.1 when you ask for one.
